chapters.title: Alas for the Day!
chapters.html:
Joel 1

What the Locust Left

1The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.

2Hear this, you elders;
give ear, all inhabitants of the land!
Has such a thing happened in your days,
or in the days of your fathers?

3Tell your children of it,
and let your children tell their children,
and their children another generation.

4What the cutting locust left,
the locust has eaten;
what the locust left,
the young locust has eaten;
and what the young locust left,
the grasshopper has eaten.

Wake Up and Weep

5Wake up, you drunkards, and weep;
wail, all you drinkers of wine,
over the sweet wine,
for it is cut off from your mouth.

6For a nation has come up against my land,
mighty and without number;
its teeth are the teeth of a lion,
and it has the jaws of a lioness.

7It has made my vine a waste
and my fig tree splinters;
it has utterly stripped it bare and thrown it down;
its tendrils have turned white.

8Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth
for the husband of her youth.

9Grain offering and drink offering are cut off
from the house of the LORD;
the priests mourn,
the ministers of the LORD.

10The field is devastated,
the ground mourns;
for the grain is devastated,
the new wine dries up,
the oil wastes away.

11Be ashamed, you farmers;
wail, you vinedressers,
over the wheat and over the barley,
for the harvest of the field has perished.

12The vine dries up,
and the fig tree wastes away;
pomegranate, palm too, and apple tree,
all the trees of the field are dried up;
for joy has dried up
from the sons of men.

Proclaim a Solemn Assembly

13Gird yourselves and lament, you priests;
wail, you ministers of the altar;
come, spend the night in sackcloth,
you ministers of my God;
for grain offering and drink offering are withheld
from the house of your God.

14Consecrate a fast;
proclaim a solemn assembly;
gather the elders,
all the inhabitants of the land,
to the house of the LORD your God,
and cry out to the LORD.

The Day of the LORD Is Near

15Alas for the day!
For the day of the LORD is near,
and it will come like destruction from the Almighty.

16Is not the food cut off
before our eyes,
joy and gladness
from the house of our God?

17The seeds shrivel under their clods;
the storehouses are desolate;
the granaries are torn down,
for the grain has dried up.

18How the beasts groan!
The herds of cattle wander in confusion,
because they have no pasture;
even the flocks of sheep bear the guilt.

19To You, LORD, I call,
for fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness,
and flame has burned up all the trees of the field.

20Even the beasts of the field long for You,
for the streams of water are dried up,
and fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.

Notes

  • v1 "The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel" — Joel names no king and no year, where Hosea and Amos name both (Hosea 1:1; Amos 1:1). Yo'el, Joel, is also the name of Samuel's firstborn (1 Samuel 8:2). For Pethuel the Greek has Bathouel, the Greek spelling of Bethuel, Rebekah's father (Genesis 24:15).

  • vv17–20 "The seeds shrivel… even the flocks of sheep bear the guilt… the beasts of the field long for You" — v17 is obscure: avshu, shrivel, megrefot, clods, and mammegurot, granaries, are found only here; the Greek has the heifers leaped at their mangers. Navokhu, wander in confusion, is what Pharaoh said of Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 14:3). Ne'shamu, bear the guilt, is the verb of now they must bear their guilt (Hosea 10:2): the flocks suffer for the guilt of men. The Greek has were destroyed, as if from nashammu, are desolate (v17), nearly the same letters. Ta'arog, long for, is the deer of As a deer longs for streams of water, so my soul longs for You, God (Psalm 42:1), with the same afiqei mayim, streams of water: the beasts pray as the prophet prays (v19).

chapters.title: I Will Pour Out My Spirit
chapters.html:
Joel 2

The LORD's Army

1Blow the horn in Zion;
sound the alarm on My holy mountain!
Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble,
for the day of the LORD is coming;
it is near —

2a day of darkness and gloom,
a day of cloud and thick darkness!
Like dawn spread out over the mountains
comes a people great and mighty;
there has never been the like of it from of old,
nor will there be again after it,
through the years of generation after generation.

3Before it fire devours,
and behind it a flame burns;
the land before it is like the garden of Eden,
and behind it a desolate wilderness,
and no one escapes it.

4Its appearance is like the appearance of horses,
and like horsemen, so they run.

5As with the noise of chariots
they skip on the tops of the mountains,
like the noise of a flame of fire
devouring stubble,
like a mighty people
drawn up for battle.

6Before it peoples writhe;
all faces grow pale.

7Like warriors they run;
like men of war they climb the wall;
they march each on his way,
and they do not swerve from their paths.

8They do not jostle one another;
each marches in his track;
they plunge through the weapons
and are not cut off.

9They leap on the city;
they run on the wall;
they climb into the houses;
they enter through the windows like a thief.

10Before it the earth trembles,
the heavens shake;
the sun and the moon grow dark,
and the stars withdraw their shining.

11The LORD utters His voice
before His army,
for His camp is very great;
for mighty is the one who does His word.
For the day of the LORD is great
and very fearful;
who can endure it?

Return to Me

12Yet even now, declares the LORD,
return to Me with all your heart,
with fasting, with weeping and with lamenting.

13Tear your hearts and not your garments,
and return to the LORD your God;
for He is gracious and merciful,
slow to anger and abundant in loyal love,
and He relents of the evil.

14Who knows? He may turn and relent,
and leave a blessing behind Him,
a grain offering and a drink offering
for the LORD your God.

15Blow the horn in Zion;
consecrate a fast;
proclaim a solemn assembly;

16gather the people;
consecrate the assembly;
bring together the elders;
gather the children
and those who nurse at the breast;
let the bridegroom go out of his room,
and the bride out of her chamber.

17Between the porch and the altar
let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep,
and let them say,
"Spare Your people, LORD,
and do not give Your inheritance to scorn,
for the nations to rule over them.
Why should they say among the peoples,
'Where is their God?'"

The LORD Answers

18Then the LORD was jealous for His land
and had pity on His people.

19The LORD answered and said to His people:
I am about to send you
the grain, the new wine and the oil,
and you will be satisfied with it;
and I will no longer make you
a scorn among the nations.

20The northerner I will remove far from you,
and drive him into a land dry and desolate,
his front into the eastern sea
and his rear into the western sea;
his stench will go up,
and his foul smell will rise,
for he has done great things.

21Do not fear, O ground;
rejoice and be glad,
for the LORD has done great things!

22Do not fear, you beasts of the field,
for the pastures of the wilderness are green;
for the tree bears its fruit;
the fig tree and the vine
give their full strength.

23You sons of Zion,
rejoice and be glad in the LORD your God,
for He has given you the early rain for righteousness;
He has brought down rain for you,
the early rain and the late rain, at the first.

24The threshing floors will be full of grain,
and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.

25I will repay you for the years
that the locust has eaten,
the young locust, the grasshopper and the cutting locust,
My great army,
which I sent among you.

26You will surely eat and be satisfied,
and praise the name of the LORD your God,
who has dealt wondrously with you;
and My people will never be put to shame.

27You will know that I am among Israel,
and that I am the LORD your God,
and there is no other;
and My people will never be put to shame.

I Will Pour Out My Spirit

28And it shall come to pass afterward
that I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh;
your sons and your daughters will prophesy,
your old men will dream dreams,
and your young men will see visions.

29Even on the male servants and the female servants
in those days I will pour out My Spirit.

30I will give wonders
in the heavens and on the earth:
blood and fire and columns of smoke.

31The sun will be turned to darkness,
and the moon to blood,
before the great and fearful day of the LORD comes.

32Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape;
for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem
there will be those who escape,
as the LORD has said,
and among the survivors
those whom the LORD calls.

Notes

  • vv4–9 "like horsemen, so they run… all faces grow pale… they enter through the windows like a thief" — the army may be the locusts of chapter 1 seen as soldiers, or soldiers seen as locusts; the chapter names it only His army (v11) and, in v25, My great army, with the four locust names. Kibbetsu pa'rur, grow pale, is uncertain, word for word gather pa'rur, perhaps a glow; the phrase is found again only in Nahum, of Nineveh. The Greek has every face like a scorched pot: parur, pot, has nearly the same letters, the word of boiled it in pots (Numbers 11:8). Yashoqqu, they leap, is the verb of as locusts leap, men leap on it (Isaiah 33:4). Houses full of them were the word to Pharaoh, Your houses will be full (Exodus 10:6).

  • vv12–14 "Yet even now… return to Me… Tear your hearts and not your garments… Who knows?" — shuvu adai, return to Me, answers Amos's refrain, yet you did not return to Me, declares the LORD (Amos 4:6), said of the locust too (Amos 4:9); with all your heart is the law's, when you return to the LORD your God with all your heart (Deuteronomy 30:10). To tear the garments is the outward sign, as Ahab tore his clothes (1 Kings 21:27). The name is the LORD's own from Sinai, God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love (Exodus 34:6), with gracious put first, and Jonah says it again in the same order (Jonah 4:2). He relents of the evil, as the LORD relented of the evil at the calf (Exodus 32:14). Who knows? is David's word as he fasted, Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me (2 Samuel 12:22). The blessing left behind is the grain offering and drink offering that were cut off (1:9, 13).

  • vv28–29 "I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh… Even on the male servants and the female servants" — in the Hebrew text vv28–32 are 3:1–5, and chapter 3 is chapter 4; the English numbering is followed. Ve-hayah acharei khen, and it shall come to pass afterward: after the rain, the Spirit. Moses had wished it, If only all the LORD's people were prophets, and the LORD would put His Spirit on them! (Numbers 11:29), and Ezekiel and Isaiah heard it promised, when I have poured out My Spirit on the house of Israel (Ezekiel 39:29), I will pour My Spirit on your seed (Isaiah 44:3). The Spirit falls on old and young, sons and daughters, and the lowest of the house, male servants and female servants, the pair of Genesis 12:16. The Greek has of My Spirit and My servants, and Peter follows it at Pentecost as far as will escape in v32, with in the last days for afterward (Acts 2:16–21).

  • vv30–32 "blood and fire and columns of smoke… everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape" — mofetim, wonders, are the signs and wonders the LORD gave against Egypt (Deuteronomy 6:22), and the smoke is Sinai's, Its smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln (Exodus 19:18); columns of smoke is the phrase of Song of Songs 3:6. The sun and moon darkened in v10 are now turned to darkness and to blood, and the great and fearful day is v11's. Calling on the name of the LORD is as old as Seth's son, Then it was begun, calling on the name of the LORD (Genesis 4:26). Yimmalet, will escape, and peletah, those who escape: none escaped the army (v3), and some will escape the day, as Isaiah heard, out of Jerusalem shall go a remnant, and survivors out of Mount Zion (Isaiah 37:32). Yiqra, calls on, and qore, calls: those who call on the LORD are those the LORD calls. The Greek has those who bring good news, whom the Lord has called.

chapters.title: The Valley of Decision
chapters.html:
Joel 3

The Valley of Jehoshaphat

1For in those days and at that time,
when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

2I will gather all the nations
and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat,
and I will enter into judgment with them there
on behalf of My people and My inheritance Israel,
whom they scattered among the nations;
and they divided up My land.

3They cast lots for My people,
and gave a boy for a prostitute,
and sold a girl for wine, and drank it.

4What are you to Me, Tyre and Sidon,
and all the regions of Philistia?
Are you paying Me back for something?
If you are doing something to Me,
swiftly and speedily I will return your deed on your own head.

5For you have taken My silver and My gold,
and carried My finest treasures into your temples.

6You sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem
to the sons of the Greeks,
to remove them far from their own border.

7I am about to rouse them from the place
where you sold them,
and I will return your deed on your own head.

8I will sell your sons and your daughters
into the hand of the sons of Judah,
and they will sell them to the people of Sheba,
to a nation far off;
for the LORD has spoken.

Beat Your Plowshares into Swords

9Proclaim this among the nations:
Consecrate war!
Rouse the warriors!
Let all the men of war draw near and come up.

10Beat your plowshares into swords,
and your pruning hooks into spears;
let the weak say, "I am a warrior."

11Hurry and come, all you nations around,
and gather yourselves there.
Bring down Your warriors, LORD!

12Let the nations be roused and come up
to the Valley of Jehoshaphat;
for there I will sit to judge
all the nations around.

13Put in the sickle,
for the harvest is ripe.
Come, tread,
for the winepress is full;
the vats overflow,
for their evil is great.

14Multitudes, multitudes,
in the valley of decision!
For the day of the LORD is near
in the valley of decision.

15The sun and the moon grow dark,
and the stars withdraw their shining.

The LORD Dwells in Zion

16The LORD roars from Zion
and utters His voice from Jerusalem,
and the heavens and the earth shake;
but the LORD is a refuge for His people,
a stronghold for the sons of Israel.

17You will know that I am the LORD your God,
who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain;
Jerusalem will be holy,
and strangers will no longer pass through her.

18And it shall come to pass on that day
that the mountains will drip sweet wine,
and the hills will flow with milk,
and all the streams of Judah will flow with water;
a spring will come out from the house of the LORD
and water the valley of Shittim.

19Egypt will become a desolation,
and Edom a desolate wilderness,
because of the violence done to the sons of Judah,
for they shed innocent blood in their land.

20But Judah will be inhabited forever,
and Jerusalem for generation after generation.

21I will hold their blood innocent,
which I had not held innocent;
and the LORD dwells in Zion.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "when I restore the fortunes… the Valley of Jehoshaphat… I will enter into judgment with them there" — in the Hebrew text this chapter is chapter 4; the English numbering is followed. Ashiv et shevut, restore the fortunes, is the law's promise, the LORD your God will restore your fortunes… and gather you again from all the peoples (Deuteronomy 30:3), and Hosea's, a harvest is appointed, when I restore the fortunes of My people (Hosea 6:11). Yehoshafat, Jehoshaphat, is the LORD's name joined to shafat, judge, and the verb follows twice: ve-nishpatti, I will enter into judgment (v2), and lishpot, to judge (v12). The valley is named for what happens in it, as the valley of Jehoshaphat's own victory was named the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed the LORD (2 Chronicles 20:26).

  • v11 "Hurry and come… Bring down Your warriors, LORD!" — ushu is found only here, and its sense, hurry or come to help, is guessed from the line. The last words are the prophet's prayer, hanchat YHWH gibborekha; for them the Greek has let the meek one be a warrior.

  • vv19–21 "they shed innocent blood… I will hold their blood innocent, which I had not held innocent" — dam naqi, innocent blood, as in so that innocent blood is not shed within your land (Deuteronomy 19:10), and v21 answers with the same root: niqqeiti, I hold innocent, is the word of I am innocent (Jeremiah 2:35). As the Hebrew stands, the LORD declares innocent the blood of Judah that had gone unanswered. The Greek has I will seek out their blood, and I will not hold guiltless. In their land may be Judah's land or Egypt's and Edom's; the verse does not say.
